answer: Pairwise uniqueness challenges stop one operator running many identities. Each epoch the registry pairs identities for a prompt; both answer together, signed by their keys, and auditors score the delta between the answers. One operator cannot fill two seats, so a fake stays silent and hits the nadir floor, or copies its twin and fails the delta test. Each identity posts a 50-credit bond, lost on failure, and a raven log records pairs. The kth fake needs a kth stand-in and bond, so 1,000 fakes cost 1,000 stand-ins and 50,000 credits, none reusable. Honest agents answer once, bonds kept.
